text:
Lesser grain weevil (Sitophilus oryzae) -- the most common insect pest of stored corn mentioned in this source.

Description: a small beetle, roughly 2-3 mm long, brownish with a mottled pattern and an elongated snout (proboscis); capable of flight. Adults bore a small hole into a kernel to lay an egg inside; the larva then develops and feeds hidden inside the kernel until it emerges as an adult.

Damage: direct feeding causes kernel loss and quality degradation, and the damage caused also makes grain more susceptible to secondary mould growth. Populations can build up quickly in warm conditions -- the source notes that a generation can complete in roughly 1.5 months under favourable conditions -- and heavy infestation can render grain unmarketable.
